# Source: https://github.com/faest-sign/faest-ref, directory tests/, tag v3.0.2
# (commit 4fb6b71143), licence MIT (see ../faest_v3_0_2/LICENSE.faest-ref).
# Upstream files and their SHA-256:
#   tests/fields.cpp            5144a709d39e72b8fde9621072c7792b9e7f91702e4be44fa8780b765ee4289b
#   tests/universal_hashing.cpp a03d0ec82a030781cc24da4dcf312b9d8b10824265c1e5aa5e0102422db11b18
#   tests/hash_shake.cpp        d78c57af4ec305ec22f834dc821bad64a7c923b7d2263394d9511c4673aa9c25
#
# Values only: every line is `name = lowercase hex` (or a decimal integer) of one
# constant array of the upstream test file, bytes unmodified and in upstream order;
# nested arrays are flattened in order. No upstream code is reproduced. The files
# were parsed as text; nothing upstream was compiled or executed.
#
# Names: `<upstream file stem>.<array name>`; arrays local to one upstream test case
# are `<stem>.<test case>.<array name>`. The GF(2^64) arrays (`enc_poly64_*`,
# `test_bf64_test_vectors`) are omitted: FAEST v3.0 has no GF(2^64) field.
#
# How the upstream tests consume them (TEST_VEC_LEN = 16, lb = lambda / 8):
#   fields.test_bf<L>_test_vectors.{lhs,rhs,expected}: expected = lhs * rhs in GF(2^L).
#   fields.test_bf<L>_test_vectors_with64.{lhs,rhs,expected}: rhs is 8 bytes, the low
#     64 coefficients of a GF(2^L) element; expected = lhs * rhs.
#   fields.enc_poly<L>_vec_{xs,ys,products}: 16 triples of lb bytes, products[i] = xs[i] * ys[i].
#   fields.poly<L>_from_8_poly1_{input,output}: output[i] (lb bytes) = ByteCombine of the
#     bits of byte input[i].
#   fields.poly<L>_from_8_poly<L>_{input,output}: input is 8 * 16 elements of lb bytes;
#     output[i] = sum over b in [0..8) of input[8 * i + b] * alpha_8^b.
#   fields.poly<L>_sum_poly_output: sum over b in [0..L) of input[b mod 128] * x^b, input
#     being the 128 elements of fields.poly<L>_from_8_poly<L>_input.
#   universal_hashing.zk_hash_<L>_{sd,xs,digest}: 4 vectors; vector i uses seed bytes
#     [i * (3 * lb + 8) ..), the 9 elements starting at element 8 * i of xs (the upstream
#     index stride is 8 elements although each vector reads 9, so consecutive vectors
#     overlap by one element) with the first 8 as x_0 and the ninth as x_1, and digest
#     bytes [i * lb ..).
#   hash_shake.shake_256.*: SHAKE256(data1 || LE32(data2)) squeezed to 32 bytes.
